title: add vpc control plane terraform: cross-account peering, route53, interface endpoints, security groups
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add multi-account VPC peering and Route53 delegation support for private control plane Terraform modules. Backwards-compatible module inputs; new optional features gated behind variables.
description: Motivation: private control plane customers frequently run control plane components in a dedicated VPC and require secure cross-account connectivity, private Route53 delegation, and service interface endpoints to avoid internet egress. This PR adds optional Terraform module primitives and examples to provision: multi-account VPC peering (including route table updates and peering auth roles), interface and gateway endpoints (S3, ECR, Secrets Manager, KMS), security group templates for control plane components, and Route53 inbound delegation with cross-account role setup. The description below summarizes the intent, user-facing inputs, and rollout considerations. Changes: added a new module modules/vpc-control-plane with submodules: modules/vpc-control-plane/peering (cross-account peering resources and aws_ec2_transit_gateway support toggle), modules/vpc-control-plane/endpoints (aws_vpc_endpoint and aws_vpc_endpoint_service configurations, interface endpoint security group rules), modules/vpc-control-plane/route53 (delegation zone, records for internal endpoints, optional private hosted zone sharing), and examples/multi-account-peering demonstrating two-account setup with example IAM role ARNs and route table attachments. All new features are opt-in via variables (enable_peering, enable_route53_delegation, enable_endpoints) with sensible defaults disabled. Implementation notes: - Uses aws_eip and aws_vpc_peering_connection for single-VPC peering and includes explicit route table attachments and conflict checks. - Cross-account peering requires a peering_requester_role and peering_accepter_role; the example provides an assume-role pattern and guidance in modules/README.md. - Route53 inbound delegation is created in the control plane account and a delegation record is created in the tenant account via an optional provider alias; documentation includes manual DNS delegation steps when automatic delegation is not permitted by policy. - Interface endpoints are created with security groups that only allow grpc/http ports from known control-plane subnets; S3 gateway endpoints include route table associations for private subnets. Testing and safety: added unit-level terraform fmt and validate CI checks, ran full plan against a smoke account with mocked ARNs, and integration smoke-test in a sandbox AWS org to validate cross-account role assumption and route propagation. Upgrade and rollback: changes are additive and gated; to upgrade, set enable_peering to true and provide peering role ARNs; rollback is performed by setting the feature flag to false and running terraform apply which tears down peering and endpoint resources. Note: peering teardown requires careful route table cleanup - we added lifecycle ignore_changes for route table association ids to avoid accidental deletion during partial upgrades. Docs and examples: updated modules/README.md and added a step-by-step example in examples/multi-account-peering/README.md including IAM policy snippets and troubleshooting tips. Follow-ups: add TGW implementation in a subsequent PR and include more automation for Route53 delegation across accounts where org-level policies allow.
